6.text: You found me! Tomorrow I’m picking a trickier branch.
6.flag: The source card says NO card for this idea (the fun is the search). Proposal: keep night 1 card-free as the PDF says, and use this note only on night 2 with the quick variation. André decides whether the page shows it at all.

7.text: Santa’s mailbox is open! Write your letter today and I’ll fly it to the North Pole tonight.

16.text: Gone fishing! The fish here are crunchy. Want a turn?

17.text: I covered your door in nice things. Every word is true!

20.text: New sled, test run tonight. Top speed: very sweet.

23.text: Practicing for Santa’s big night. Rate them too — do we agree?

28.text: Official news from the North Pole: you made the Nice List!
28.flag: The certificate itself is the message (no card in the source). Proposal: print this line at the top of the certificate instead of a separate card; the page block would read “Elf note — on the certificate”.

30.text: Thank you for a wonderful December. Only Santa can touch me tonight — see you next year!
30.flag: Short version for the page block; the full farewell letter is in printables.farewellLetter.

elfNotes._rule: D5 — the ideas whose elfNote is null in ideas.json (verified: 6, 7, 16, 17, 20, 23, 28, 30). Short, in the elf’s voice, matching only what the scene has.

wouldYouRather.rule: 24 questions = one printable set (source card step 3). Question 1 is verbatim from the source; 2–24 are new drafts. One card per day, December 1–24.

questions.text: Would you rather ride a reindeer or drive the sleigh?
Would you rather build a snowman or have a snowball fight?
Would you rather have a nose that glows like a reindeer’s or ears that jingle like bells?
Would you rather wrap presents with Santa or decorate cookies with the elves?
Would you rather live in a gingerbread house or in an igloo?
Would you rather be as tiny as an elf for a day or as tall as the Christmas tree?
Would you rather have hot cocoa with marshmallows or with whipped cream?
Would you rather find a mountain of snow outside your door or a mountain of presents under the tree?
Would you rather sing a Christmas song in front of everyone or dance to one?
Would you rather have a pet reindeer or a pet penguin?
Would you rather wear pajamas covered in candy canes or a sweater covered in tinsel?
Would you rather spend a day in Santa’s workshop or a night riding in the sleigh?
Would you rather have a snowball that never melts or a cookie that never runs out?
Would you rather be the star on top of the tree or a present underneath it?
Would you rather go ice-skating with a polar bear or sledding with a penguin?
Would you rather have Christmas lights in your hair or jingle bells on your shoes?
Would you rather eat breakfast at the North Pole or dinner at the South Pole?
Would you rather make the toys in the workshop or test them all?
Would you rather talk to reindeer or understand what snowmen say?
Would you rather open one present every day or all of them on Christmas morning?
Would you rather have a snow day every Monday or a cocoa party every Friday?
Would you rather be the elf for a day or have an elf as your friend all year?
Would you rather decorate the tree with candy or with paper snowflakes?
Would you rather have pointy elf ears for a week or a jingling hat for a week?

farewellLetter.rule: Source card step 1 and 3: it says thank you, mentions 2 real moments of the child’s year, promises to come back, and explains that only Santa can touch the elf at the farewell. Blanks are filled in by the parent.
text: Tonight is my last night with you this year, and I want to say thank you. Thank you for the giggles, for the good mornings and for looking for me every single day.
I will always remember when you ________________________________, and the day you ________________________________. Both are going straight into my North Pole memory book.

Tonight Santa comes to take me home. Here is a little secret: at the farewell, only Santa can touch me. That is how the magic gets me safely back to the North Pole. So tonight, just a big wave from your bed!
Keep the little frame somewhere you can see it. Every time you look at it, I will be thinking of you too.
I promise to come back next December. Be kind, keep laughing, and save me a cozy spot by the tree.

storyCard.rule: Keeps the source opening line and its 5 blanks in the same order (a noun, a place, a food, an animal, a verb). No blanks added.
storyCard.text: Last night, the elf rode a [1. a noun] to the [2. a place] ... When it got there, it was so hungry that it ate a whole [3. a food] in one bite. Then a sleepy [4. an animal] came over and asked to join the adventure. So the two of them decided to [5. a verb] all the way home before the sun came up. Shh — don’t tell Santa!

kindnessMissions.rule: 12 missions, one per card, inside the “TOP SECRET MISSION” envelope. 1 is verbatim from the card; 2–4 come from the card’s own rotation (step 3); 5–12 are new drafts. Nothing needs scissors, heat, cooking or going out alone.

missions.text: Today: draw a picture for someone you love.
Today: pick a toy to donate.
Today: say thank you to someone.
Today: make a card for a neighbor or a friend.
Today: give three people a compliment.
Today: help a grown-up tidy up — without being asked.
Today: share a toy or a snack with someone.
Today: read a story to a younger kid or to a stuffed animal.
Today: let someone else go first.
Today: give someone in your family a big hug and tell them why you love them.

clueTrail.rule: 4 clue cards in sequence from the bed to the hiding spot (source card). Clue 1 is the verbatim starting card. Clues 2–4 are new and generic: the parent writes the next place in the blank. The hiding spot must be visible for the child’s age (source step 1).

clues.text: I'm back... but where? Follow the clues and find me before breakfast!
clues.source: ideas.json (verbatim) + a new “First stop” line so card 1 also points to a room — flag

clues.text: Not here! I tiptoed off to the ____________. Your next clue is waiting there.
Getting warmer! Now hurry to the ____________ and look around.
Last clue! I’m hiding near the ____________. Listen for the jingle bell!

optionalHints._rule: Optional one-line hints a parent can copy under the blank instead of naming the room. Places taken from the source card (bookshelf, tree, low shelf) plus common rooms.
optionalHints.kitchen: Where the cookies live and the cocoa gets made.
optionalHints.living room: Where the family sits for movie night.
optionalHints.tree: Where the lights twinkle all night long.
optionalHints.bookshelf: Where the stories sleep side by side.
optionalHints.low shelf: Look down low — lower than your knees!
optionalHints.front door: Where the boots and shoes wait for morning.

hooks._rule: C6(b) — one line under the title (source document §4: “1 line saying the child’s reaction”). Max 90 characters. Playful, true to the idea’s own data.

movie-night-popcorn-patrol.text: They wake up to find the elf already hogging the remote for movie night.

storytime-reading-corner.text: Little ones find the elf reading to their stuffies — and want to listen too.

shoe-shoe-train.text: The hallway turns into the North Pole Express — and every shoe has a passenger.

toothbrush-delivery-elf.text: A brand-new toothbrush, delivered by elf — suddenly everyone wants to brush.

tangled-in-christmas-lights.text: The elf tried to decorate. The lights won. Expect giggles at breakfast.

hiding-in-the-christmas-tree.text: Where’s the elf? Kids spend breakfast spotting a tiny face in the branches.

letter-to-santa-station.text: The elf opens a mailbox to the North Pole — and the letters start pouring in.

trapped-in-a-jar.text: Kids find the elf stuck in a jar — and beg to rescue it before breakfast.

christmas-countdown-chain.text: One link a morning: kids count down to Christmas with the elf’s paper chain.

sleeping-in-a-stocking.text: The elf overslept in the stocking — little ones will want to tiptoe and whisper.

flour-snow-angel.text: “It snowed in the kitchen!” Kids find a tiny snow angel and its proud artist.

toilet-paper-tree-makeover.text: Caught in the act: the elf “decorated” the tree, and kids will laugh before hello.

marshmallow-bubble-bath.text: The elf is having a spa day in marshmallows. Do not disturb (but do giggle).

toothpaste-mirror-message.text: A minty message on the mirror from the elf — and suddenly everyone wants to brush.

silly-banana-bunch.text: Every banana has a face this morning — toddlers will want to name them all.

sink-fishing-trip.text: Gone fishing! Kids find the elf reeling in crackers at the sink — and want a turn.

sticky-note-surprise-wall.text: A door full of sticky notes — and a few of them say what’s great about your kid.

elf-zipline-adventure.text: The elf took the express route to the cookies — kids will want to see it zip.

sweet-spaghetti-breakfast.text: Spaghetti with syrup for breakfast? Kids get to decide if the elf is a genius.

candy-cane-sled.text: The elf built a sled out of candy canes — and it’s ready for a sweet test run.

hot-cocoa-stand-helper.text: Cocoa costs one hug at the elf’s stand — expect a line of customers.

cookie-baking-disaster.text: Tiny floury footprints lead to the culprit — and a cookie with one bite missing.

milk-and-cookies-taste-test.text: The elf is practicing for Santa’s big night — and kids get to be the cookie judges.

gingerbread-house-inspector.text: Official inspection results are in: the roof is delicious. Kids will agree.

kindness-mission-card.text: A top secret mission arrives — and it’s all about being kind today.

candy-cane-scavenger-hunt.text: Five candy canes, one elf dare: can they find them all before breakfast?

build-a-snowman-challenge.text: The elf’s snowman record is 2 minutes. Your kid will want to beat it.

nice-list-certificate.text: They wake up to official proof they made the Nice List — with their name on it.

would-you-rather-card.text: Reindeer or sleigh? Breakfast turns into a big debate, started by the elf.

farewell-letter-and-photo.text: A thank-you letter and a keepsake to hold on to — a goodbye that feels warm.

im-back-arrival-banner.text: The elf is back — with a banner, a marker and a big hello for the whole family.

north-pole-arrival-breakfast.text: The elf’s first move? An extra-tiny pancake breakfast, made just for you.

special-delivery-arrival-box.text: A package from the North Pole at the front door — and someone is peeking out.

arrival-hide-and-seek-clue-trail.text: The elf is back… but where? Kids follow the clues room by room to find it.

snowy-footprints-arrival.text: Snowy little footprints from the door — the elf was too excited to wait.

toddler-peekaboo-blanket-fort.text: Peekaboo! Toddlers find the elf in a blanket fort — then hide it again together.

pom-pom-color-sorting-game.text: The elf started sorting colors and needs a helper — toddlers are on it.

breakfast-cereal-garland.text: The elf made a necklace you can eat — toddlers will want to add the next ring.

my-first-sticker-scene.text: The star is too high for the elf — toddlers get to finish the tree themselves.

toy-car-wash-station.text: The elf opened a car wash — and toddlers are first in line with their cars.

plush-friends-campout.text: A sleepover in their own room — toddlers find the elf snuggled in with the stuffies.

fruit-face-breakfast-plate.text: Breakfast is smiling back today — and the elf helped make the face.

elf-workshop-build-station.text: The elf’s workshop shift started overnight — kids will want to finish the toy.

paper-snowflake-window-invasion.text: The elf ordered snow — and the whole window got delivered overnight.

mini-elf-door-and-welcome-mat.text: The elf finally has its own front door — kids will want to knock.

cardboard-sleigh-build.text: A backup sleigh built from a box — the elf says it passed the test drive. Mostly.

gingerbread-village-street.text: There’s a new mayor in town — kids wake up to a whole gingerbread street.

elf-photo-booth-props.text: The elf opened a photo booth — and today your kid is the model.

elf-story-fill-in-the-blanks-card.text: The elf wrote a story but left out the words — kids fill in the silly ones.

elf-workout-challenge-cards.text: North Pole training starts at breakfast — the elf already did one. Sort of.

guess-how-many-jar.text: How many are in the jar? The elf’s guess is wild — kids are sure they can win.

draw-my-outfit-contest.text: The elf wants a new look — and your kid is the designer today.

flour-snowball-fight.text: Snowball fight on the counter! The teddies started it, according to the elf.

bubble-bath-foam-mountain.text: The elf asked for a little foam and got a mountain — expect big laughs.

wrapping-paper-mayhem.text: The elf wrapped the living room for Santa — even the TV remote.

elf-in-the-fridge-surprise.text: Open the fridge and surprise: the elf is in there, shivering in a scarf.

fridge-magnet-message.text: One letter is missing from the elf’s fridge message — kids get to finish it.

closet-fashion-show-elf.text: Fashion week came to the bedroom — and the elf is wearing the look.

memory-jar-last-week-goodbye.text: A jar of favorite moments — kids add one each day of the elf’s last week.

goodbye-breakfast-and-hug-coupon.text: One goodbye hug, today only — the sweetest coupon of the whole season.

tonightFallback.currentExample: **No exact match tonight** — here are 5 minutes, no mess ideas. We left out “Only stuff I have” to find you 3.
tonightFallback.proposed: **No exact match tonight.** We let go of {dropped} — here are 3 that still {keptPhrases}.
tonightFallback.proposedAllDropped: **No exact match tonight.** We let go of {dropped} — here are 3 from all 60 ideas.
tonightFallback.joiners: Dropped labels in curly quotes joined by “ and ”; kept phrases joined by “ and ”.
examples: **No exact match tonight.** We let go of “Only stuff I have” — here are 3 that still take 5 minutes or less and make no mess.
